# Native explicit-target file publication

The Unix publisher receives an absolute file target explicitly selected by its caller and one declared path that requests must match. It retains the selected parent directory and refuses existing links or non-regular targets. Path and complete-content budgets precede publication effects. Targets ending in `/`, `/.` or `/..` are rejected before path normalization.

An exclusive nonblocking selected-parent lock coordinates native publishers for the duration of staging, replacement and cleanup. A refusal preserves the prior target and creates no temporary entry. Explicit saves intentionally replace the target currently present; later completed saves win, including when several retained publisher handles select the same target. This is replacement authority rather than a compare-and-swap API. Writers outside the native protocol do not participate in its advisory lock.

The candidate is written into an exclusive private staging directory beneath the selected parent. The adapter verifies its owner, 0700 mode and opened identity, retains its descriptor, creates the candidate exclusively, writes/flushed/syncs its complete bytes and closes the file. Candidate identity checks and the final rename use that retained private descriptor. Swapping the staging directory entry in the parent therefore cannot substitute the candidate. Staging cleanup removes the held candidate and removes the selected staging entry only while its identity still matches; it never removes a substituted directory. No fallible publication result follows successful replacement. REQ-0752 and REQ-0753 now explicitly permit this protected staging namespace on the target filesystem.

Eight native integration tests cover complete/empty/UTF-8 bytes, unchanged old hard-link aliases, path/capacity refusal, directory suffixes, link/directory refusal, retained selected-parent authority after rename, lock refusal with explicit retry, intentional replacement by a later completed save and observed permission failure. DAC tests restore permissions and report privileged bypass. A deterministic adapter unit test swaps the temporary entry immediately before rename; it failed by publishing replacement bytes before correction and now publishes the original checked bytes through the retained descriptor. The lock refusal also failed before correction.

The private R bridge registers handles without dereferencing user pointers. Owned build results save through the native engine gate with no source recapture or R publication callback. Installed replay compares complete reports for all seventeen unchanged original results, exact successful CSV bytes, retained Parquet bytes, repeated saves, capture counters and failed-build gates. It also checks bounded raw transport, target spelling and expired handles with Python absent from PATH. The bridge's roxygen comments document these private closures.

Study-source approved roots retain their separate existing rules. The public facade, Windows publication, general publication diagnostic projection and complete migration acceptance remain open. The private staging directory and its writer protocol are qualified on the checked hosts; wider filesystem/security support is not a release-matrix promise.
